question: A student had 14 reference books initially. She removed 8 outdated books, leaving 6. She added 30 new books, reaching 36. She divided into 2 equal libraries of 18 books each. She removed 4 books for repair. Her roommate has 50 books (separate collection). How many books remain in her collection?

A store had 117 items in inventory. They removed 109 items for a sale, leaving 8. They removed 2 more for customer requests, leaving 6. They multiplied by 6 to order replacement stock to 36 items. They added 25 items from a shipment, reaching 61. Her manager handles 50 items (separate inventory). How many items total does the store have now?

A warehouse started with 85 boxes. They increased 9 times to 765 boxes. They multiplied 4 times more to 3,060 boxes. They added 66 boxes, reaching 3,126 boxes. They multiplied by 4 again to 12,504 boxes. They multiplied by 3 more times for final projection to 37,512 boxes. The facility has 50,000 box capacity (not exceeded). How many boxes are projected?

A trader had 170 shares initially. She added 50 shares through purchases, reaching 220 shares. She multiplied by 7 times to 1,540 shares. She expanded 8 times more to 12,320 shares. She divided equally in half for two accounts of 6,160 each. Converting to Canadian dollars at rate 1.35 was separate calculation. Her colleague had 300 shares (separate account). How many shares total does she hold?

A student started with 54 pages of notes. She divided in half to 27 pages for review. She multiplied by 8 times to 216 pages. She expanded 6 times to 1,296 pages. She doubled to 2,592 pages for comprehensive study. She added 47 pages of new material, reaching 2,639. She removed 1,856 outdated pages. How many current pages remain?

A project began with 48 tasks. She multiplied by 9 times to 432 tasks. She removed 375 lower-priority tasks, leaving 57. She multiplied by 5 again to 285 tasks. She added 52 tasks from new requirements, reaching 337. She removed 190 tasks deferred to next quarter. Her colleague has 100 tasks (separate project). How many tasks total does she have?

A business had 145 clients in the morning. It added 49 new clients by midday, reaching 194. By afternoon, it lost 172 clients, leaving 22. It lost 5 more clients, leaving 17. It added 1 new client, reaching 18. It doubled their remaining portfolio to 36 clients. His competitor had 100 clients (separate). How many clients total does the business have?

A warehouse had 209 boxes initially. In the morning, they removed 149, leaving 60. By midday, they added 20, reaching 80. In the afternoon, they removed 8, leaving 72. They multiplied by 6 to 432 boxes. They divided equally into 6 shipments, each with 72 boxes. They doubled to 144 boxes in the final inventory. How many boxes are in the final count?

A portfolio began with 123 units. They added 79 units, reaching 202. They added 42 more, reaching 244. They added 21 final units, reaching 265. They multiplied by 5 to 1,325 units. They removed 214 units for diversification, leaving 1,111. How many units remain in the portfolio?

A project manager had 108 tasks. They multiplied by 8 to 864 tasks. They added 32 new tasks, reaching 896. They divided equally in half to 448 tasks per phase. They added 25 tasks, reaching 473. They doubled the workload to 946 tasks. Converting to weekly targets involved separate calculation. How many total tasks does the manager oversee?

A retailer started with 160 items. They added 39 items, reaching 199. They added 43 more, reaching 242. They multiplied by 7 to 1,694 items. They added 4 final items, reaching 1,698. The warehouse had 3,000 item capacity (not exceeded). How many items total does the retailer have?

A collector had 80 items. They multiplied by 4 to 320 items. They expanded 5 times to 1,600 items. They divided equally in half to 800 items per category. They doubled the inventory to 1,600 items. Her colleague had 200 items (separate). How many items total does the collector have?

A student started with 223 pages. In the morning, they added 59 pages, reaching 282. By midday, they divided into 6 equal study groups of 47 pages each. In the afternoon, they removed 37 pages for corrections, leaving 10. By evening, they removed 6 more pages, leaving 4. They added 36 pages of review materials, reaching 40. How many pages total does the student have?

A warehouse had 178 boxes. In the morning, they removed 124, leaving 54. In midday, they removed 1 more, leaving 53. In afternoon, they added 48, reaching 101. By evening, they removed 73, leaving 28. They multiplied by 8 for shipment projection to 224 boxes. How many boxes are projected?

A warehouse started with 98 boxes. In the morning, they removed 60, leaving 38. By midday, they doubled to 76 boxes. In the afternoon, they removed 26, leaving 50. By evening, they removed 30, leaving 20. They multiplied by 8 for shipment to 160 boxes. They removed 104 for delivery. How many boxes remain?

A project started with 55 tasks. They multiplied by 4 to 220 tasks. They removed 88 completed tasks, leaving 132. They removed 129 deferred tasks, leaving 3. They added 68 new urgent tasks, reaching 71. They added 54 more, reaching 125. Converting hours needed was a separate calculation. How many tasks total are pending?

A student started with 27 pages initially. They removed 3 outdated pages, leaving 24. They multiplied by 5 to 120 pages. They added 43 new pages, reaching 163. They added 73 more reference pages, reaching 236. Their classmate had 100 pages (separate set). How many pages total does the student have?

A business started with 52 clients in the morning. In midday, they lost 45 clients, leaving 7. In afternoon, they doubled to 14 clients. They multiplied by 5 to 70 clients. They removed 59 for account review, leaving 11. They added 67 new referrals, reaching 78. Her colleague manages 30 clients (separate). How many clients total does the business have?

A factory started with 31 units. They multiplied by 4 to 124 units. They expanded 6 times to 744 units. They added 57 units, reaching 801. They divided equally into 3 production lines of 267 each. The facility has 1,000 unit capacity (not exceeded). How many units per line?

A collector started with 14 items. They added 25 items, reaching 39. They multiplied by 6 to 234 items. They added 74 more, reaching 308. They added 58 final items, reaching 366. Her friend has 100 items (separate). How many items total does the collector have?

A manager started with 72 employees. In the morning, they added 34, reaching 106. By midday, they multiplied by 8 to 848. In the afternoon, they expanded by 3 times to 2,544. They removed 252 through reorganization, leaving 2,292. They multiplied by 3 for a future projection to 6,876. How many employees are projected?

A business started with 203 revenue units. They added 69, reaching 272. They removed 24, leaving 248. They multiplied by 7 to 1,736 revenue units. They lost 1,253 in an incident, leaving 483. Converting to annual revenue involves separate calculation. How many revenue units remain?

A business had 240 clients initially. They multiplied by 7 to 1,680. They added 29, reaching 1,709. They multiplied by 5 to 8,545. They multiplied by 4 to 34,180. They added 79, reaching 34,259. They doubled to 68,518. Converting to market size was separate analysis. How many total clients are projected?

A student had 96 notes initially. They added 29, reaching 125. They added 27 more, reaching 152. They removed 131 duplicates, leaving 21. They multiplied by 9 to 189 notes. They divided equally into 3 study groups of 63 each. How many notes per group?

A collection started with 25 items. They doubled to 50. They tripled to 150. They removed 131 broken items, leaving 19. They multiplied by 6 to 114 items. Using displays for storage was separate consideration. How many items total does the collection have?
